title: Menu Design Meets Market Design: Strategic Simplicity vs. Choice Complexity
abstract: arXiv:2611.17984v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Strategic simplicity removes the incentive to misreport preferences, but it does not ensure that participants can identify what they prefer. We study this distinction in a laboratory experiment on serial dictatorships, where optimal play only requires choosing one's favorite bundle of real-effort tasks. Participants make fifteen incentivized choices among bundles that vary in how many tasks they combine. They choose either from a large menu or through a series of binary choices. Having made all choices, they unexpectedly reconsider each assignment against a previously rejected alternative. We find that roughly one in six choices is reversed and almost one in five involves an objectively dominated bundle. Simplifying the choice architecture does not help. Binary decomposition even raises reversal rates among low-ability participants and further inflates their confidence about their choices.

translated_title: 菜单设计与市场设计的交汇：策略性简约与选择复杂性
translated_abstract: 策略性简约消除了误报偏好的激励，但并不能确保参与者能够识别自己真正偏好什么。我们在一个关于序贯独裁机制的实验室实验中研究这一区别，在该机制中最优策略只需选择自己最喜欢的真实努力任务组合。参与者在任务数量各不相同的组合之间进行十五次有激励的选择，他们要么从大菜单中选择，要么通过一系列二元选择进行挑选。在完成所有选择后，他们意外地被要求将每个分配方案与之前被拒绝的替代选项进行重新比较。我们发现大约六分之一的选择被推翻，近五分之一的选择涉及客观上被占优的组合。简化选择架构并无帮助：二元分解甚至在低能力参与者中提高了推翻率，并进一步膨胀了他们对自己选择的信心。
tldr: 通过序贯独裁机制的实验室实验，本文发现即使在策略性简约环境下，约六分之一的选择仍被推翻，而简化选择架构（如二元分解）不仅无助于减少选择错误，反而加剧了低能力参与者的错误并膨胀其过度自信。
en_tdlr: Using a serial dictatorship lab experiment, this paper shows that even under strategic simplicity, roughly one in six choices is reversed, and simplifying choice architecture—such as binary decomposition—does not reduce errors but instead increases reversal rates and inflates overconfidence among low-ability participants.
